identity.title: ALMA-SZ Detection of a Galaxy Cluster Merger Shock at Half the Age of the Universe

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA measurements of a merger shock using the thermal Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (SZ) effect signal, at the location of a radio relic in the famous El Gordo galaxy cluster at $z \approx 0.9$.

why_this_method.value: uv-fitting avoids biases from imaging a diffuse low S/N negative signal

evidence.quote: The $uv$-fitting method safeguards against possible biases that can occur when imaging a diffuse, low S/N negative signal like a cluster shock in SZ.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Global weak-lensing mass prior rejected as inaccurate for a disturbed sector, replaced by X-ray pressure prior

evidence.quote: for a merging cluster like El Gordo a global mass prior will be inaccurate for modeling the pressure in a disturbed sector, so we derive a pressure prior from the X-ray data.

limitations_admitted.value: Short-spacing problem makes Mach number anti-correlated with pressure normalization

evidence.quote: its amplitude is anti-correlated with the pressure normalization. This is an inherent limitation of the current ALMA observation

limitations_admitted.value: Pre-shock temperature unconstrained in Chandra data

evidence.quote: the pre-shock temperature in this high-$z$ object remains unconstrained due to the high background-to-cluster photon ratio
